# Decision log and corrections {#sec-decisions}

Everything below was decided on 2026-09-23 unless noted. Corrections are listed
explicitly. A project like this is only trustworthy if its mistakes are visible.

## Decisions

| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository | New, separate `canes-cfb-analytics` | Extend `cfb-canes-analytics` | Notebook-first project with its own scope |
| Organization | One folder per **market type**, one notebook per period | Folder per period | Keeps models of the same kind together |
| Benchmark | Sportsbook lines only | Exchanges (Kalshi, Polymarket) | Scope requested; exchange references removed from the repo |
| First target | **Points per team** | Game total, spread | One model yields spread, total and winner |
| Split | **By time**: train 2016–23, validate 2024, test 2025 | Random 80/20 | Random splits leak the future |
| Data first | ESPN (free) for games and quarters, CFBD for lines and efficiency | CFBD only | Could start before the API key existed |
| Final points model | Random forest on the ratings residual | Stacking, XGBoost | Best on 2024 validation (within noise) |
| Market layer | Dropped | Keep | Spreads failed; the totals result wasn't using the model |
| Real money | **No**; paper-trade two pre-registered rules through 2026 | Bet now | Edge not proven; the market is more accurate on average |
| Weekly runs | GitHub Actions | Local cron, manual | Runs with the Mac off; commits give tamper-evident timestamps |
| Totals model (#10) | **Not adopted**; keep rule B; skip A-vs-B conflicts | Adopt the nonlinear totals model | It overfit (2021–23 gains vanished in 2024–25); the one-line rule held |
| Preseason features | **Adopted** (portal, recruiting, new coach, preseason AP) | Keep the model as is | Early-season gap down in both decision and check seasons |
| Improvement rounds 2–3 | **Nothing adopted**; average-of-6 kept as a shadow model | Adopt the best-looking candidate | Pre-registered rule: ≥2 of 3 seasons better and a bootstrap interval above zero |
| Weekly card | English, sports-app layout, private page | Spanish, spreadsheet-style | Easier for a non-expert to use |
| Period lines (#4) | Build models now, buy lines later | Buy history now ($119) or forward only ($30/month) | See whether period models predict well first |

: Main decisions. {#tbl-decisions}

## Corrections: things that were wrong and got fixed

1. **Ratings were over-shrunk.** The first ridge ratings used $\alpha = 25$ and came out
   with a spread of about ±1.3 points, when real team differences are about ±15. Tuning
   found $\alpha = 1$ (@tbl-ridge-grid).
2. **A stale feature file.** The first ablation run used features built *before* the
   $\alpha$ fix, so "ratings alone" showed 10.4 instead of 9.44. The inconsistency with
   the tuning grid gave it away; the table was rebuilt and rerun.
3. **Notebook ordering bug.** The feature notebook once saved a v1-only table over the
   full one, which broke the backtest downstream. Sections were separated, and v1
   experiments now use `cumulative_sets(include_v2=False)`.
4. **Lint "fixes" deleted notebook imports.** Ruff's autofix removed "unused" imports
   from empty notebook skeletons. The unused-import rule is now disabled for notebooks
   only.
5. **"The totals result is a 2025 artifact."** The market layer's 55.7% on 2025 totals
   was first dismissed as an under-heavy year. The season-by-season analysis showed a
   stable shootout-under effect from 2021 to 2025. The dismissal was partly wrong, and
   the effect became rule B.
6. **"Since 2019."** The shootout effect was first described as holding every season
   since 2019; 2020 was 51.7%. The accurate statement: every season from 2021 to 2025.
7. **Ranges in the backtest notes** were rounded too generously (for example "49–50%"
   when a threshold reached 48.4%). They were replaced with the exact ranges.
8. **Opening lines availability.** The early "vs open" backtest was described as
   covering 2019–2023; opening lines only exist from 2021, so it covered 2021–2023.

9. **Swapped moneylines faked a gold mine.** The first moneyline backtest showed +12% to
   +42% ROI. It was 2.1% of moneylines with home and away swapped. After filtering them:
   −4.5% (@sec-reportcard).
10. **A missing experiment log.** A lint error stopped the command that wrote the rounds
    2–3 log, while the commit message said it was included. It was written afterwards.
11. **A too-simple calibration check.** A fixed 5-point threshold flagged one bin (said
    45%, happened 40%, 492 games) that is only 2.3 standard errors off. The check now
    uses the average miss and a z-score, and reports that bin as "Review", not hidden.
12. **Week 4 picks re-logged.** After the preseason features were adopted, week 4's paper
    picks were re-logged with the new model before any kickoff; the first version is in
    git history.

## What the evidence says, plainly

- The market is **more accurate** than the model at both the open and the close.
- Spread signals **flip sign** between seasons: noise.
- Two totals signals survived a held-out check. Neither is statistically decisive yet,
  and both are tracked on paper.
- The model's disagreement with the opener predicts **line movement** (positive CLV)
  every season. That's the most robust signal found so far.
